criteria.given: a batch whose requests all pass validation and deduplication, containing 5 LOW requests, and a configured cap of 2
criteria.then: the accepted queue contains exactly 2 LOW requests plus every non-LOW request, and exactly 3 problems with code ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP are reported — nothing is silently dropped

criteria.given: LOW requests L1..L5 with distinct requestedAt instants and a cap of 2
criteria.when: the prioritize stage applies the cap
criteria.then: the kept LOW requests are the 2 with the earliest requestedAt; the other 3 are reported as problems, and this holds for all 100 shuffles of the same batch (the kept set of requestIds is identical every time)

criteria.given: more LOW requests than the cap where several share the same requestedAt (e.g. cap 1 and LOW requests 'B-2' and 'A-1' both at 2026-10-20T08:00:00Z)
criteria.then: the tie is broken by requestId ascending, so 'A-1' is kept and 'B-2' is reported over cap — the same comparator the sorter already uses (priority weight desc, requestedAt asc, requestId asc)

criteria.given: a cap of 1 and a batch with 1 LOW, 3 MEDIUM, 2 HIGH and 2 CRITICAL requests
criteria.then: no problem is produced and all 8 requests are accepted: only Priority.LOW counts against the cap and non-LOW requests are never capped, however many there are

criteria.given: two duplicate requests whose group's highest priority is MEDIUM, so the kept request is escalated from LOW to MEDIUM, and a cap of 0
criteria.then: the escalated request is not counted as LOW and is accepted; the priority used for the cap is the priority as it stands after the deduplicate stage

criteria.given: a configured cap of 0 and a batch of 2 LOW and 1 HIGH request
criteria.then: the accepted queue contains only the HIGH request and both LOW requests are reported with ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP — a cap of 0 is a legal configuration meaning 'no Low work accepted'

criteria.given: a LOW request with requestId 'WR-9' at input index 4 that is over a cap of 2
criteria.when: the problem for it is created via Problem.overLowPriorityCap(4, "WR-9", 2)
criteria.then: the Problem has inputIndex 4, requestId 'WR-9', code ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP, null field, null relatedRequestId, null escalatedFrom and escalatedTo, and message exactly "WR-9 exceeds the per-batch Low-priority cap of 2" (the message names the request id and never the input index)

criteria.given: a batch that also produces validation and duplicate problems plus 2 over-cap LOW requests at input indices 7 and 3
criteria.when: the processing result's problems are read
criteria.then: problems appear in stage order (validate, then deduplicate, then prioritize) and, within the prioritize stage, by input index ascending — so the index-3 over-cap problem precedes the index-7 one

criteria.given: a cap of 1 and LOW requests 'L-2' and 'L-3' reported over cap
criteria.then: its stage is "prioritize", in is the number of requests received by the stage, out is the number kept (in minus 2), and its notes are one note per over-cap request of the form "L-2 dropped: over Low-priority cap of 1", sorted in natural order and containing no input indices

criteria.given: a batch with no LOW request over the cap (including an empty batch and a null batch)
criteria.then: no OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP problem is produced, the prioritize trace has in == out and no cap note, and the trace still has exactly three entries: validate, deduplicate, prioritize

criteria.given: an application context with no app.batch.max-low-priority set in configuration
criteria.then: maxLowPriority() is 1000 (via @DefaultValue("1000") on the new second record component) and maxSize() keeps its 5000 default; the WorkRequestSorter bean in ProcessingConfig is constructed with BatchProperties.maxLowPriority()

criteria.given: configuration app.batch.max-low-priority = -1
criteria.when: the properties are bound or BatchProperties is constructed directly
criteria.then: an IllegalArgumentException is thrown with message "app.batch.max-low-priority must be at least 0, was -1"; 0 and any positive value are accepted

criteria.given: existing code and tests that call new BatchProperties(5000), new WorkRequestSorter(), and new WorkRequestProcessor(validator, resolver, sorter)
criteria.when: those are compiled and run after the change
criteria.then: they still compile and behave as before: BatchProperties(int maxSize) delegates to maxLowPriority 1000, and the no-arg WorkRequestSorter() applies no cap (unlimited); the capped behaviour is reached only through new WorkRequestSorter(int maxLowPriority)

criteria.given: the default configuration and the 13-request sample batch in sample-batch.json
criteria.then: the accepted queue, problems and trace counts (13 → 10 → 6) are unchanged, because the default cap of 1000 exceeds the number of LOW requests in it

criteria.given: a batch generated to cover every problem kind, now including over-cap LOW requests, processed with a cap small enough to be exceeded
criteria.when: the result's problems are inspected and BatchObserver records the batch
criteria.then: every ProblemCode value — including OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP, appended last in the enum — appears at least once, and BatchObserver increments one counter per ProblemCode value with no hard-coded code list left behind

outOfScope: Caps for MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL priorities, or a cap on total accepted requests (app.batch.max-size already guards batch size)
Per-sender, per-equipment or per-time-window fairness quotas — the cap is per batch and global to the batch
Adding a fourth pipeline stage or a fourth StageTrace entry; the trace stays validate, deduplicate, prioritize
Rejecting or failing the whole batch (HTTP error, InvalidBatchException) when the cap is exceeded
Introducing a java.time.Clock bean or any time-based staleness rule
Changing the sorter's ordering rules, the duplicate/escalation rules, or validation
Runtime/per-request override of the cap via API parameter, header or request body field
New DTO fields or response shape changes; the new code travels through the existing ProblemDto.code string
Editing sample-batch.json or re-pinning SampleBatchTest expectations
